summary: After the accepted underwater coin fix, the selected v41 replay has no screen or cursor mismatches; its first remaining RNG divergence is at step 81 in monmove.c:set_apparxy. That function matches source. C vision.c:vision_recalc restricts underwater COULD_SEE to adjacent pool squares, while JS vision_recalc still uses ordinary view_from. The first guessed square is adjacent ordinary floor, so JS accepts it and skips the C retry draw.

source.branch: When the hero is underwater outside the water level, vision_recalc suppresses night vision and marks only valid pool squares in the surrounding 3-by-3 area as both IN_SIGHT and COULD_SEE. The preceding Blind and Rogue-level branches retain precedence. The subsequent x-ray overlay still applies.
callers: allmain.c:moveloop() builds the initial visibility map with vision_recalc(0); JS allmain.js:moveloop() does the same.
allmain.c:moveloop_core() recalculates after commands when vision_full_recalc is set (lines 471 and 542); JS allmain.js:moveloop_core() recalculates at its corresponding turn boundaries.
monmove.c:dochug() and m_move() call set_apparxy(); JS monmove.js:dochug() and m_move() call set_apparxy(), which reads couldsee from the published vision array.
dependencies: The existing vision bitmap, dbridge.c:is_pool port, and monmove.c:set_apparxy implementation. No set_apparxy implementation change is required.

evidence: The saved queue entry at .cache/latest-saved-combined-queue.json (SHA-256 7505fb24cd01792c8cb781d651dd66ffaa451361e46f7c456fd2705afde0a43a) identifies batch v41, case v41-underwater-coin-flip-drops-coin, recording challenges/cases/v41/v41-underwater-coin-water-nymph-seven-pages-corrected.session.json (SHA-256 eb1f3e6ac92b42a22c4387ccea87b1bc168e7ba597c68f92035ff4534c48ce79), manifest challenges/manifests/v41.json (SHA-256 7f6627032def2f88334c51f8372f9b61e908665fa995f5d24b06af89532acc69), and evaluation challenges/evaluations/accepted-0acc8a59f86065f8ff2d90ca1decab45701746e8-v41.json at 0acc8a59f86065f8ff2d90ca1decab45701746e8.

At step 81 (key "$"), the C recording calls rn2(20)=5 from trap.c:water_damage line 4771 before the monster action. The original evaluation has 81/82 screens and 2664/2720 RNG matches with 82/82 cursors; the first screen mismatch is the gold total, C 0 versus JavaScript 1.

Fresh run run-zsLkLx of node scripts/diff-fresh.mjs challenges/cases/v41/v41-underwater-coin-water-nymph-seven-pages-corrected.recipe.session.json reproduces the same step-81 boundary: C has 2720 RNG calls and JavaScript has 2675; C’s first call is rn2(20)=5 from trap.c:water_damage:4771 while JavaScript’s next call is rn2(3)=2. Screens are 81/82 with the differing gold count, and cursors are 82/82.

Upstream src/apply.c:4527-4556 establishes that Underwater selects lose_coin, prints “It tumbles away.”, calls dropx(otmp), and returns before the ordinary face-flip draw. Upstream src/do.c:789-797 passes an ordinary non-swallowed drop through dropy/dropz; src/do.c:161-357 handles a pool landing by calling water_damage(obj, NULL, FALSE) and returns whether it was destroyed.

The missing call is explicit in js/apply.js:5171-5174: the underwater lose_coin branch records note_unported("do.c dropx underwater") instead of invoking dropx. The ordinary downstream implementations already exist in js/do.js, but preflight_dropx rejects underwater state at line 1925 and pool terrain at lines 1973-1975. This source trace identifies the needed implementation as removing the underwater coin-flip refusal and admitting ordinary non-boulder objects through the existing pool/lava drop/flooreffects routes without conditioning on coin class or a session coordinate.

After the implementation, fresh run run-IQFe1s on the selected v41 recipe reports 82/82 screens and cursors matching. The first RNG mismatch is call 2665 at monmove.c:set_apparxy:2258 during the subsequent monster phase, after apply.c:flip_coin and trap.c:water_damage have returned. Thus the named flip_coin divergence has moved past the function, while this recording still has a later RNG mismatch.

Independent runtime evidence: recipes/apply.c/flip-coin-underwater-pool-independent.session.json uses seed 41040138, a new date, and a distinct character identity. Its committed C recording matches a fresh differential in run-fXhEQh: 2541/2541 PRNG values, 55/55 screens, 55/55 cursors, and no animation frames. The production input reaches doapply COIN_CLASS dispatch, flip_coin underwater loss, dropx, pool flooreffects, and water_damage.

priorAcceptedWork.summary: The earlier apply.c:flip_coin fix and test correction are accepted. This follow-up investigates the later RNG mismatch exposed after that fix.

followupEvidence: Saved queue SHA-256 7fe4c4f5d1d0efa7adc3cd87e577bff05524109dea78c72d19e02fc572c62676 identifies synthetic/v41/v41-underwater-coin-flip-drops-coin, recording challenges/cases/v41/v41-underwater-coin-water-nymph-seven-pages-corrected.session.json (SHA-256 eb1f3e6ac92b42a22c4387ccea87b1bc168e7ba597c68f92035ff4534c48ce79), manifest challenges/manifests/v41.json (SHA-256 7f6627032def2f88334c51f8372f9b61e908665fa995f5d24b06af89532acc69), and accepted evaluation at 9c5253b9dcd9d1469e4f5a8cf3a73c04694bbd8b.

The accepted v41 queue result has 82/82 screens and 82/82 cursors matching, with 2668/2720 RNG calls matched. At segment 0, step 81, key "$", the first remaining mismatch is call 2664: C rn2(3)=2 from monmove.c:set_apparxy:2258 while JavaScript calls rn2(5)=0 in distfleeck.

Source trace of monmove.c:set_apparxy (2198 onward) and js/monmove.js:set_apparxy (2252 onward) shows the same underwater radius-one x/y draws, accessibility checks, and final couldsee rejection. The first chosen coordinate is (11,2) for hero position (11,3).

A temporary runtime trace on the accepted JavaScript implementation confirms couldsee(11,2) returns true with terrain type 25 (not a pool) and COULD_SEE|IN_SIGHT bits set. C vision.c:589-610 instead enters its Underwater branch and assigns visibility only when is_pool(col,row) is true, so C rejects this candidate and consumes the retry draw.

JS vision.js:727-789 contains a source comment identifying underwater vision as unported; vision_recalc computes underwaterOutsideWaterLevel but then still calls view_from. Its later night-vision guard already suppresses night vision underwater. C vision.c:512-622 establishes branch precedence: swallowed/control 2, Blind, Rogue level, underwater, then ordinary view_from.

followup.status: source cause confirmed; implementation scope not yet claimed
